$comment: Branch protection on `main` as GitHub enforces it (GET repos/CandleViewer/CandleViewer/branches/main/protection, 2026-10-18; its ruleset rules, GET repos/CandleViewer/CandleViewer/rules/branches/main, 2026-10-31). Every setting the API reports is declared here, because a full PUT replaces the whole object. scripts/check_branch_protection_drift.py compares each one with the live state and proves that `ci-required` judges every CONSTITUTION.md C-9.1 check (scripts/check_required_check_reconciliation.py). Its weekly run (governance-drift.yml) has not compared anything yet: the GH_BRANCH_PROTECTION_TOKEN secret it reads is not provisioned (docs/ci-runbook.md), so it stops at 'token not found'. Owner item: add that secret, a fine-grained token for this repository with read-only Administration access. Nothing requires the `governance` workflow, which runs the GOV-00x checks and these scripts' tests on every PR. Owner item: add {"context": "governance", "app_id": 15368} to required_status_checks.checks (the merge queue is on, so it must also report on merge_group, which only pr.yml does since #3536), or make it a lane `ci-required` judges. scripts/apply_branch_protection.py only prints its changes unless given --apply. It refuses unknown keys and a lockout (a required check no workflow reports, or an approval no agent can give), and refuses a change that weakens the live protection unless given --allow-weaken. `$` keys are notes. `branch` and `pending_checks` are never sent or compared, and `merge_queue` is compared with the ruleset rules on `main` and never sent. `merge_queue` is the merge queue rule of the ruleset on `main`, with the rulesets API's parameter names and the values read live on 2026-10-31: the owner turned the queue on 2026-10-19/20, squash-merging, grouping ALLGREEN (the merge commit built for each entry must pass `ci-required`, not only the group's head), 3 builds in parallel, up to 5 entries per merge, a lone entry merging at once (minimum 1, no wait), and a 60-minute check timeout. pr.yml runs on merge_group since #3536 (#3433), so every merge passes a merge_group run; a pull request's own `ci-required` is not the full set while the PR is a draft, because the e2e, a11y and engine-bench lanes are deferred until it is ready (ADR-0013 Amendment 5, #5154). scripts/apply_branch_protection.py writes no ruleset, and refuses while the rules on `main` differ from this file. The drift check and the apply script compare every active rule on `main` with this file, which can declare only merge_queue. The same ruleset also carries a required_status_checks rule (`ci-required`, strict false) that this file cannot declare, so until they learn that rule type the drift check reports it as drift (rules.required_status_checks, unexpected_on_live) and apply refuses (#5177); no other ruleset may apply to `main`. $deviations names each setting that falls short of the Constitution and the owner item that closes it.

$deviations.required_status_checks: C-9.1 requires its checks on `main` branch protection, by names that match the job names in .github/workflows/. GitHub requires one check, `ci-required` from GitHub Actions (app 15368): the ADR-0013 rule 2 resolver, which fails unless every applicable lane passed. The reconciliation proves that every C-9.1 check except pending_checks is a lane it judges, mapping the names that differ. It proves wiring only: that such a lane runs, not that the lane's content meets that check's gate. Owner item, one of: amend C-9.1 to say its checks are required through `ci-required`; or keep C-9.1 as written, give each C-9.1 name a job that always reports its lane's result (as `architecture` does for the py lane), and require those names here. CONSTITUTION.md is unchanged. strict is false, so a PR's own run can be green against an older `main`: a risk to C-4.2, `main` releasable at every commit. The merge queue closes it: it is on for `main` (the `merge_queue` block, 01-sdlc-and-branching.md section 7), so every merge passes a `merge_group` run of `main` plus the PR, which pr.yml supports since #3536.
$deviations.required_pull_request_reviews: C-4.1 expects GitHub to require reviews and dismiss stale approvals on new commits, and ADR-0013 binding rule 1 asks for two approvals including one code owner. The agents share the owner's GitHub account, and GitHub does not count an author's own approval, so any count above 0 would block every merge while enforce_admins is true. Instead, C-10.1's two independent reviews are recorded on the PR and checked against the head commit by the delivery orchestrator's merge guard. Owner item: amend C-4.1 and Appendix A's C-10.1 row to name that guard, or give reviewers their own accounts, then set 2 approvals, code-owner review, last-push approval and stale-review dismissal. Until then scripts/apply_branch_protection.py refuses a required approval, code-owner review or last-push approval as a lockout.
$deviations.required_conversation_resolution: C-10.7 and 01-sdlc-and-branching.md section 6.1 say an unresolved review thread blocks merge. GitHub does not enforce that today. Owner item: set this to true.

pending_checks.$comment: C-9.1 checks with no wiring yet: no lane `ci-required` judges runs them, and none is a required check of its own. Read only by the reconciliation, which proves wiring only and fails on a C-9.1 check that is neither wired nor listed here, and on an entry that is wired now.
pending_checks.bundle-size: No PR workflow runs size-limit or scripts/check-bundle-size-regression.mjs. #3080 wires it into CI, in a lane that `ci-required` judges.
pending_checks.pr-metadata: pr-metadata.yml is a separate workflow so that title, body and label edits re-run it, which means `ci-required` cannot judge it. Owner item (#2280): add {"context": "pr-metadata", "app_id": 15368} to required_status_checks.checks, and, as the merge queue is on, make pr-metadata.yml report on merge_group too (#3536 did that for pr.yml only).
